paraphrase: Appearances are mind, and emptiness is mind; realization is mind and delusion is mind; arising is mind and ceasing is mind — may all doubts about mind be cut.
notes: Reference from memory; the text is not available locally. Verse number not certain.

paraphrase: When the unobstructed power of love arises for beings who suffer through not realizing this, the empty essence shines nakedly in the midst of compassion: may we practise the union of emptiness and compassion unceasingly.
notes: Reference from memory; the text is not available locally. Verse number not certain.

paraphrase: The prayer ends its account of meditation with aspirations for the experiences and realizations of the path — free of attachment to bliss, clarity and non-thought — culminating in non-meditation.
notes: Reference from memory; the text is not available locally. Recalled only in outline.

paraphrase: The ground of purification is mind itself, clarity and emptiness inseparable; the purifier is the great vajra yoga of Mahāmudrā; what is purified are the adventitious stains of delusion; the fruit of purification is the stainless dharmakāya.
notes: Reference from memory; the text is not available locally. Verse number not certain (c. v.6–7).

paraphrase: It is not existent — even the victors do not see it; it is not non-existent — it is the basis of all saṃsāra and nirvāṇa; this is not a contradiction but the middle way of union — may we realize the nature of mind, free of extremes.
notes: Reference from memory; the text is not available locally. Verse number not certain (c. v.9–10).

paraphrase: Not realizing this, beings circle in saṃsāra; realizing it, buddhahood is nothing other than this; there is no 'this is it' or 'this is not it' — may we realize the nature of dharmatā, the all-ground.
notes: Reference from memory; the text is not available locally. Verse number not certain; wording recalled loosely.

paraphrase: The waves of coarse and subtle thought subside in their own place and the river of mind rests unwavering in its natural state; free of the stains of dullness and torpor, may the ocean of śamatha be stable. Looking again and again at the mind that cannot be looked at, may we see vividly what is not seen, just as it is, and cut doubts about what is and is not.
notes: Reference from memory; the text is not available locally. Two consecutive verses, numbers not certain.

paraphrase: Confidence in the view is cutting through doubts about the ground; the key of meditation is to sustain that without distraction; the supreme conduct is to train in the meaning of meditation in everything — may we have the view, meditation and conduct.
notes: Reference from memory; the text is not available locally. Verse number not certain.
